 Yolo County reminds property owners of Dec. 10 property tax deadline

 By Daily Democrat | Daily Democrat PUBLISHED: October 26, 2026 at 1:30 PM PDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 The Yolo County Tax Collector’s Office is reminding property owners that the first installment of 2026-27 secured property taxes is due Nov. 1 and will become delinquent if not paid by Thursday, Dec. 10. A 10% penalty will be added to payments made after the applicable deadline.
 Taxpayers have several ways to pay:
 Online or by phone: Pay by electronic check at no charge, or by credit or debit card with a 2.34% convenience fee. Visit the Yolo County Property Tax webpage and select “Pay Property Tax,” or call (877) 590-0714. Electronic payments must be completed by 11:59 p.m. on December 10. Taxpayers are encouraged to pay several days in advance because transactions can take up to three business days to process.
 By mail: Payments must be postmarked by the U.S. Postal Service on or before December 10 to avoid the penalty.
 In person: Payments may be made at the Yolo County Tax Collector’s Office, 625 Court Street, Room 102 in Woodland. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and will remain open until 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, December 10.
 Yolo County also partners with Easy Smart Pay, a private payment service that allows property owners to spread their property tax payments across monthly installments. Payments made through a bank account have no transaction fee, while credit and debit card payments carry a 1.99% fee.
 Enrollment for the Dec. 10 tax installment closes Nov. 30. To learn more or enroll, visit easysmartpay.net/yolo-ca.
 Under California law, failure to receive a property tax bill does not relieve a property owner of responsibility for payment or any resulting penalties. Property owners who have not received a tax bill should contact the Yolo County Tax Collector’s Office as soon as possible at (530) 666-8625 or TaxInfo@YoloCounty.gov.
 Property taxes help fund local governments and public agencies, including schools, cities, the County, community colleges, rural fire districts and cemetery districts. More than half of property tax revenue supports local schools, while rural fire districts rely on property taxes for more than 90% of their annual funding. Yolo County receives about 9% of total property tax revenue, or approximately 9 cents of every dollar paid.
